posts.title: Start Over, or Cut It Out
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: On six months of writing and the roughly two thousand readers who found posts I made almost impossible to find, the ambiguity of an AI moment that feels hopeful and doomed at once, and the fork I keep returning to with my brother's product — make surgical cuts you can't fully trace, or start over and inherit a fresh pile of technical debt — and why, either way, the human stays accountable for what to keep and what to cut.

posts.title: Remember Long Enough, Forget Fast Enough
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: On a compliance job where LLMs multiplied the work, the night Fable 5 arrived and then vanished for foreign nationals, and a Deutsche Welle documentary about remembering long enough and forgetting fast enough — why the model is the better memory and we're the better forgetting.

posts.title: Our Limitations Give More Than They Take
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: A line from Al Hirschfeld about limitations being the only value in art, read at 23, set against today's push to give AI complete freeway — on supply-chain attacks, a pre-commit hook you install yourself, and why knowing your limits is what keeps a developer relevant.

posts.title: When the LLM Thinks Too Fast
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: On parallel Claude and Copilot loops, a QA skill, and two weeks of letting the LLM run everything — and why the result is a maze.

posts.title: Software Developers Can Sell You the Next Big Thing
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: On the surprise of technical founders who can sell, the shift from building to overseeing, and whether a developer can pitch not the structure of the code but something they imagine happening.

posts.title: AI Should Do My Laundry
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: On flows, relevance, and a backlog skill for Claude — turning the tedious sorting of sprint planning into something AI can do while we get back to the actual work.

posts.title: Who Is Your Information Broker
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: When two AIs agree on something wrong and only a human catches it — exploring the gap between what AI appears to know and what it actually knows, and why asking where the information comes from is the most important skill in an AI-assisted workflow.

posts.title: Do Machines Understand Machines
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: From Google Stitch to Claude's honest critique — exploring what happens when AI designs for developers, and why the human filter still matters.

posts.title: When Designers Become QA: The Hidden Cost of AI-Driven Workflows
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: Exploring how AI integration is pushing designers into QA roles they aren't equipped for, and why design documentation needs to include testable requirements alongside mockups.

posts.title: Laravel Sail + Cloudflare Tunnel: A Production-Grade Development Setup
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: A complete guide to running Laravel 12 with Sail behind a Cloudflare Quick Tunnel — with Vite HMR, queue workers, scheduler, and Laravel Reverb WebSockets all working through a single public URL.

posts.title: Nonsensical Jargon for Something to Pass
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: From Sokal's postmodern hoax to AI-generated code - exploring how jargon can mask meaninglessness, and why human oversight remains crucial in software development.

posts.title: How Polymorphism Morph to Anything
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: A personal journey of becoming a father and implementing a newsletter system for a static blog - exploring the intersection of life changes, AI, and software development polymorphism.

posts.title: How pressure metrics works
posts.author: Marin Nikolli
posts.excerpt: A personal journey from childhood curiosity to creating arra.blog - exploring early memories from Albania and the spark that ignited a passion for learning and technology.
